subject: general
question: The current population of a town is 20,000. It increases by 30% and 50% in two successive years but decreases by 68% in the third year. What is the population of the town at the end of the third year?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Successive percentage change can be calculated using the multiplying factor method directly.

⇒ Final Population = Initial Population × (1 + 30/100) × (1 + 50/100) × (1 − 68/100)

⇒ Final Population = 20,000 × 1.3 × 1.5 × 0.32

⇒ Final Population = 20,000 × 0.624 = 12,480

**∴ The correct answer is 12,480.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Initial Population = 20,000

First year change = +30%

Second year change = +50%

Third year change = −68%

**Formula Used:**

A = P × (1 ± R₁/100) × (1 ± R₂/100) × (1 ± R₃/100)

**Calculations:**

⇒ Population after 1st year = 20,000 × (1 + 30/100) = 20,000 × 1.30 = 26,000

⇒ Population after 2nd year = 26,000 × (1 + 50/100) = 26,000 × 1.50 = 39,000

⇒ Population after 3rd year = 39,000 × (1 − 68/100) = 39,000 × 0.32 = 12,480

**∴ The correct answer is 12,480.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Successive Percentage Change

When a value is subjected to two consecutive percentage changes of x% and y%, the net percentage change can be derived using: Net Change = x + y + (x × y) ÷ 100.

Multiplying Factor Method

For sequential changes, the final value can be obtained by chaining multiplying factors. An x% increase means multiplying the base by (1 + x ÷ 100) and a y% decrease means multiplying by (1 − y ÷ 100).

Base Change Concept

In successive percentage problems, each new percentage must be calculated on the newly updated value of the previous step (the new base), not on the original starting value.
